races.name: Try Unibet's New Improved Acca Boosts Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Pageant Girl
runners_data.note: Has a course-winning profile and races prominently, sitting ideally between the pace battle and the hold-up pack; her win came over 6f at Good going and the slight surface slowdown is not an obvious concern with blinkers fitted.|
runners_data.comment: Pageant Girl has struggled in her last three starts, finishing fifth, seventh, and eighth, and her rating of 64 leaves her ranked tenth of twelve on our figures. She has run over today's trip before and a win four starts back offers slim hope.

runners_data.name: Kochella
runners_data.note: David Egan takes the ride on this hold-up filly who has shown a solid 6f effort (3rd at Goodwood); the strong gallop projected here suits a horse that wants to come from off the pace, and she has no obvious going concern.|
runners_data.comment: Kochella showed plenty when finishing third three starts back, has run over today's trip, and returns on a good 21-day break with our rating nudging above her official mark — the risk is that her two most recent efforts have been disappointing.

runners_data.name: Beach Ahead
runners_data.note: One of three confirmed front-runners who will battle for supremacy from the off; a tongue-tie is fitted and Gary & Josh Moore strike at only 1/18 in the past 14 days, meaning the yard is not in a hot vein — being in that pace war on Standard to Slow ground after 59 days off is a significant ask.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last two starts and ranked last on our figures, Beach Ahead has been off the track for 59 days and has questions to answer on current form; he has run over today's trip before, and draw five is noted.

runners_data.name: Tallahassee Lassie
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride on a filly with a win to her name and progressive form; her prominent style positions her perfectly to track the front-runners without joining their battle, and 6f looks an adequate test given her 5f wins — she is a leading contender for Scenario B.|
runners_data.comment: Tallahassee Lassie arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip, with 22 days between runs suggesting she's been given time to recover properly; the risk is that her earlier finishes of fifth and sixth show some inconsistency in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Nascent Star
runners_data.note: Robert Havlin partners this consistent front-runner whose form figures of 4-4-0 suggest he finds trouble closing, and being dragged into a three-way pace war on a slower surface is an obvious trap — Hugo Palmer's yard is at 4/35 in the past fortnight, offering some stable support.|
runners_data.comment: Twice fourth in recent starts, Nascent Star arrives here in solid fitness at 18 days since his last run, has experience over today's trip, and our figures suggest he's working off a lenient official mark — a live contender despite being yet to win in his last three.

runners_data.name: Najmet Minzaal
runners_data.note: Callum Rodriguez on a prominent-style runner who has been hitting the frame consistently (4-4-5) without winning; crucially, his one run on a similar Standard surface produced a win/place of 0W0P in three attempts, questioning his AW suitability here.|
runners_data.comment: Najmet Minzaal has shown consistent mid-pack form — fourth two starts back and fourth again three starts back — and has run over today's trip, while 28 days off should leave her fresh; the concern is she's yet to win in her last three starts.

runners_data.name: Crowned
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes a lightly raced filly (just two runs) who has placed at 3rd and 4th without landing a blow — she is an unknown quantity and her trainer operates at 0/12 in the past 14 days, meaning there is little confidence to draw from the yard at this moment.|
runners_data.comment: Placed third two starts back but only fourth last time out, Crowned has run over today's trip and steps up on his official mark on our rating, though he remains winless in recent starts and the 41-day absence may blunt his sharpness.

runners_data.name: Its A Ginger Thing
runners_data.note: Finley Marsh on a hold-up type who is tagged as a horse that fades in the finish — that profile is a direct mismatch with a Scenario A close finish, and 11 days between runs is a brisk turnaround for a horse already flagged for late weakening.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts — fifth last time out, and eighth three starts back — Its A Ginger Thing has run over today's trip and returns on a quick 11-day turnaround, though his official mark of 63 and draw two suggest he faces a stiff ask from mid-division.

runners_data.name: Invincible Isaac
runners_data.note: A hold-up runner who has managed only a single top-5 finish from five races and whose record on Standard going (0W0P in one attempt) does not encourage confidence on this surface; the visor is fitted but trainer Lemos De Souza is at 0/6 in the past 14 days.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Invincible Isaac steps back up having shaped with some promise when fifth two starts back, though a sixth last time out and a ninth three starts back temper expectations; experience over today's trip and going offers some encouragement from stall six off a 34-day break.

runners_data.name: Secret Rival
runners_data.note: Kieran Shoemark partners one of the three front-runners, but Secret Rival's form figures of 8-6-7 are consistently poor, and Ed Walker's yard is firing at 10/34 in the past fortnight — the jockey-trainer combination has support, but this horse has to improve markedly to justify front-running ambitions.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts — a run of sevenths and eighths punctuated by a sixth — Secret Rival heads into this rated 62 and ranked near the foot of our assessments, though she has run over today's trip before and a trainer firing at 29% is a genuine positive.

runners_data.name: Time And Effort
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa picks up the ride on a runner whose best run came over this exact trip on a Standard surface (2nd at Kempton), making him the most AW-proven horse in the field on similar going; Ivan Furtado is modestly active but the course-and-distance form is the key angle here.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked ninth of twelve on our figures, Time And Effort faces a stiff ask here, with a struggling trainer (1/23 over the last 14 days) and 130 lb from stall 10 adding little encouragement — though she has run over today's trip and was second last time out.

runners_data.name: Trust Yourself
runners_data.note: James Doyle takes a hold-up filly who is flagged for fading in the finish — a potential contradiction given her profile suits a pace-collapse scenario, though her form figures of 0-0-6 over 5-6f on Good ground have not shown the finishing kick needed here; 39 days off adds further uncertainty.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, Trust Yourself heads here 39 days on from a sixth last time out, with two unplaced efforts before that; he has run over today's trip and our rating of 68 gives him a chance, though 130 lb from stall 12 makes life harder.

races.paceDynamic: Nascent Star, Beach Ahead, and Secret Rival are all confirmed front-runners in a 12-runner nursery over 6f on a Standard to Slow Kempton AW surface, guaranteeing a fierce early battle for supremacy and a genuinely strong gallop from the outset. With three horses all wanting to lead, none will get a free or uncontested rail, meaning sectional times will be fast and the pace will be honest rather than manufactured. The Standard to Slow going further drains stamina reserves, compounding the energy cost on any horse that has burned fuel in a front-running battle. This race shape strongly favours hold-up and midfield horses who can conserve energy in the early stages and produce a late, sustained run into a flattening field — closers and stalkers with proven finishing kicks are best positioned to capitalise on what looks like a pace-collapse finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the three-way pace battle burns out the front-runners inside the final two furlongs, hold-up horses sweep through a tiring field.
scenarios.body: The frantic early pace set by Nascent Star, Beach Ahead, and Secret Rival ensures the leaders are spent by the time they reach the final furlong on a slower-than-standard surface, handing energy-conserving hold-up runners a clear route through. Horses who have shown late finishing ability and are comfortable at 6f on AW surfaces are perfectly profiled for this outcome.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent-style runners tracks the pace at a comfortable distance and outkicks rivals in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A horse like Tallahassee Lassie or Pageant Girl, tracking the war without being embroiled in it, could inherit the race as front-runners fold, needing just enough stamina to hold on through the final 100 yards.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Steals Race
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three front-runners breaks cleanly, secures a lead without a serious early challenge, and dictates on a solo basis.
scenarios.body: Should Beach Ahead or Nascent Star gain a decisive early advantage before the others assert, they could potentially control fractions and steal enough margin to hold on, though Standard to Slow ground makes this materially harder to sustain over 6f.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind, Late Burst
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is only moderately strong and the race sets up as a grinding stamina test where midfield runners pick off tiring rivals.
scenarios.body: A truly muddling or grinding tempo — less likely given three confirmed front-runners — could compress the field and allow a midfield type like Crowned or Time And Effort to make late ground, though neither has demonstrated sufficient finishing authority at this level yet.

watchPoints.text: Watch the three-way battle between Nascent Star, Beach Ahead, and Secret Rival in the first two furlongs — whichever horse is forced to race widest at pace will be the one most likely to capitulate dramatically, leaving the race wide open for hold-up horses.|

Kochella is held up but has only three runs to her name and has never raced on an AW surface — if the slow surface catches her out, even a well-set pace scenario will not produce a winning run from David Egan.|

Tallahassee Lassie carries Oisin Murphy but has only won over 5f — the step up to 6f on a Standard to Slow surface is an untested combination, and if she doesn't get cover behind the pace she could be left exposed too early.|

Time And Effort's placed form at Kempton on Standard going is the most directly relevant course-and-distance evidence in the field — monitor his early position, as Silvestre De Sousa ideally needs him to travel prominently without being embroiled in the front-runner war.|

Its A Ginger Thing has returned quickly (11 days) and carries a late-fading flag — in a race almost certain to require a sustained finish, backers should be aware this horse is statistically likely to be the one dropping away inside the final furlong.|

races.name: Unibet/British Stallion Studs EBF Novice Stakes (Div I) (GBB Race)

Unibet 3 Uniboosts A Day Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Becky Burke Memorial Novice Stakes (Div I) (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Purple Moon
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett-trained — wait, George Baker runner — returned from 118 days off to win on soft ground over 10f last time and now faces AW for the first time; prominent style suits the expected controlled pace perfectly, and the 1m3f trip looks an ideal step up.|

runners_data.name: Anchor
runners_data.note: Clare Hobson's hold-up filly has only one run on record (7th of 16f at Goodwood) after 134 days absent; Gina Mangan takes the ride and the standard pace may not generate the late run the hold-up profile requires.|

runners_data.name: Barachiel
runners_data.note: A five-year-old hold-up type with a string of disappointing efforts at 16f on Good ground and one distant finish on soft; the drop back to 1m3f on AW looks speculative, and the pace scenario does not obviously suit.|

runners_data.name: Digger One
runners_data.note: Josephine Gordon partners this prominent-style five-year-old who is flagged as a fader in the finish — a concern at 1m3f on a track that rewards horses who sustain their effort; four runs show a consistent pattern of dropping away late.|

runners_data.name: Arklan
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's lightly raced three-year-old has only a fifth at 12f on Good ground on his card and carries an unknown style flag; Callum Hutchinson claims and the gelding's lack of form makes assessment difficult, though the trip extension is interesting.|

runners_data.name: Be Hopeful
runners_data.note: Sean Levey partners this Menuisier-trained front-runner who has finished 11th and 7th on the flat on standard going over shorter trips; confirmed leader here and the uncontested position is his chief asset, though his form suggests he is yet to find real winning form.|

runners_data.name: Centrum
runners_data.note: Colin Keane rides this Gosden-trained three-year-old who has run twice on similar AW going and is flagged as a fader — the blinkers noted in headgear may sharpen his concentration, but his tendency to come home in arrears is a live concern over 1m3f.|

runners_data.name: Dialstone
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's lightly raced three-year-old ran a promising second at 10f on Good ground; Rossa Ryan takes over and the step up to 1m3f on AW under Standard To Slow conditions looks a logical progression for a horse who may have more to offer.|

runners_data.name: Fortitudine
runners_data.note: James Doyle partners this Charlie Appleby debutant — stable with an excellent record introducing juveniles and three-year-olds on AW; no form to assess and going marked unknown, but the Appleby/Doyle combination at Kempton demands respect.|

runners_data.name: Mid Flight
runners_data.note: Robert Havlin rides this three-year-old returning after a huge 271-day break; the horse has run on standard going before but the lengthy absence and the hold-up style in a race with a controlled pace creates significant uncertainty, and the visor is noted.|

runners_data.name: Treble Bass
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's lightly raced three-year-old showed a modest sixth at 10f on Good last time after 16 days; Ray Dawson rides and the unknown style flag means tactical positioning is unclear, though the trainer's track record with unexposed types warrants attention.|

runners_data.name: Westender
runners_data.note: David Menuisier's hold-up three-year-old returns after a remarkable 377 days off the track; the fading flag and a finishing position of 11th on the only start over 7f on Good suggest a horse who has not yet found his feet, and the layoff adds significant risk.|

races.paceDynamic: Be Hopeful is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 12-runner field and, ridden by Sean Levey for David Menuisier, is expected to take up the lead uncontested from the outset on Kempton's flat polytrack circuit over 1m3f. The prominent types — Purple Moon, Digger One, and Centrum — will settle just behind but none have the profile to seriously dispute the pace, meaning Be Hopeful can dictate a controlled, measured tempo rather than a scorching gallop. Standard To Slow conditions on the all-weather surface will further blunt any tendency for the pace to stretch the field, rewarding a horse that travels sweetly close to the action rather than one forced to make up a large deficit late. This race shape distinctly favours prominent-to-close-up stalkers who can track Be Hopeful within striking distance and pounce in the straight, rather than genuine hold-up horses who will find the pace insufficient to string out the field and create the late gap they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front Sets Up Stalkers
scenarios.trigger: If Be Hopeful leads at a steady Standard-To-Slow tempo and the field travels in a compact bunch, allowing close-up trackers to pounce off the final bend.
scenarios.body: Be Hopeful dictates an unhurried pace that keeps the field together, and the first or second horse off the pace — travelling within a length or two — hits the line hardest as the sprint develops from 2f out on Kempton's flat straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Capitalises
scenarios.trigger: If Be Hopeful's rivals fail to close the gap turning for home and the steady tempo proves deceptively quick enough to sustain his lead.
scenarios.body: Be Hopeful, untroubled throughout and having stolen first run on a flat track that suits a front-runner who can relax, simply holds on as the hold-up horses find the pace too even to cause a late collapse.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely slow enough that hold-up horses travel with exceptional ease and produce a strong sustained finish from 2f out.
scenarios.body: Dialstone or Fortitudine, lightly raced and potentially still improving, could benefit from tracking the pace unobtrusively before producing a sweeping late run; however, genuine hold-up types are at a structural disadvantage in a steady-pace Kempton 1m3f contest.

watchPoints.text: Be Hopeful — watch whether Sean Levey settles the leader at a genuinely controlled gallop or is tempted to inject pace early; his tempo will define the entire race shape and determine whether closers can get involved.

Centrum — Colin Keane may use the blinkers to switch this Gosden-trained prominent type on and attempt to travel more kindly than on his last two starts, which would make him a bigger threat turning for home if the fade tendency is corrected.

Fortitudine — James Doyle introducing a Charlie Appleby debutant at Kempton on AW is a combination that regularly produces well-backed, ready-to-run newcomers; watch market moves and early tracking position in the parade ring.

Dialstone — Rossa Ryan stepping up Beckett's promising second-placer to 1m3f for the first time; if the horse travels smoothly in midfield under the slow early pace, it is well placed to make a forward move two furlongs out when others may be tiring.

Westender — a 377-day absence for a three-year-old who has only run once is a significant unknown; watch for signs of freshness or reluctance in the preliminary stages as an indicator of race-readiness.

races.name: Becky Burke Memorial Novice Stakes (Div II) (gbb/gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Cloud Forest
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Saeed bin Suroor and Oisin Murphy, who can exploit an uncontested lead on this flat circuit; last two runs over 10f in Goodwood ground are shorter/softer than today's 1m3f Standard to Slow, so the step up in trip and synthetic surface represent the key unknowns.|

runners_data.name: No Ordinary Joe
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up horse aged 10 who is tagged as a finisher that fades late, and 73 days off the track is a concern; best form is over far longer distances (20f+) so this 1m3f looks short of his optimum stamina range.|

runners_data.name: Cuff It
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Richard Spencer who won a 10f soft-ground novice last time; steps up to 1m3f on AW for the first time but the synthetic surface and front-tracking style mean he is well positioned to take advantage if Cloud Forest weakens.|

runners_data.name: Atlas Mountain
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type for Alan King and Jack Mitchell who has placed three times from four starts; modest OR of 80 is well below the field's norm but he stays in contention at a compressed pace and could be a each-way factor at a price.|

runners_data.name: Kudos Too
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Muir & Grassick, last seen 22 days ago finishing mid-pack over 10f on good ground; needs pace to collapse ahead of him on a flat track but his youth (3yo) and proximity to the front in a slow-run race could see him emerge from midfield.|

runners_data.name: Shadow Road
runners_data.note: Lightly raced (one run only, 4th over 7f on Standard) with unknown stamina for 1m3f; style is unclassified, going is fine on AW, but the absence of form over this trip and distance makes him genuinely hard to assess — David Egan's booking is the one positive.|

runners_data.name: Wreck It Ronnie
runners_data.note: Style and going are both unknown due to no recorded runs, making this runner almost impossible to place in any shape; Charlie Pike's yard is 0/9 over 14 days and there is no form data to work with at all.|

runners_data.name: Angel Breeze
runners_data.note: Long-absent after 252 days off the track, and finished 9th and 14th in her only two runs on AW Standard; her natural instinct is to race deep in the field, though in this field shape she is unlikely to get to the back of the pack where she would be most comfortable — that dislocation from role tempers her chance materially.|

runners_data.name: Church Wedding
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's filly placed on her only start over 8f Standard and arrives after 203 days off; she is a prominent racer who should slot in behind Cloud Forest and could be sharper than rivals returning from a long break given Beckett's record of producing horses fit first time up.|

runners_data.name: Dove Tale
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden's hold-up filly has been off for 277 days and finished 9th on her only start over 7f soft; the combination of extreme absence, a flat circuit that limits finishers, and a fading tendency at the line makes her very hard to favour.|

runners_data.name: Persian Flaw
runners_data.note: Lightly raced unclassified type for David Menuisier and Sean Levey, with one run on Standard Polytrack (5th over 11f); the step back to 1m3f from 11f is minor and the AW form is the most directly relevant, though she has yet to show the finishing speed this shape will require.|

races.paceDynamic: Cloud Forest is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 1m3f contest on a Standard to Slow Polytrack surface and, with no obvious challenger for the lead, Oisin Murphy can dictate a controlled, unhurried gallop from the front without ever being pressured. Cuff It and Church Wedding will push forward to dispute the prominent spots just behind, but neither is likely to disturb Cloud Forest's supremacy at the head of affairs. The hold-up contingent — No Ordinary Joe, Kudos Too, Dove Tale and Angel Breeze — will be funnelled toward the rear on a flat circuit where the absence of an uphill finish limits the premium on late acceleration; the Standard to Slow surface further compresses finishing kicks. This shape heavily favours a front-runner or close-tracking prominent type who can steal ground through the final bend and maintain a winning advantage, rather than a deep closer who needs a genuine pace collapse. The field contains more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Angel Breeze, though a natural hold-up horse, has been redistributed to a midfield position because that space is occupied; the horses most likely to secure their natural prominent positions behind Cloud Forest are Cuff It and Church Wedding.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cloud Forest Dictates Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Cloud Forest is allowed an uncontested lead and controls the tempo throughout the 1m3f trip.
scenarios.body: Oisin Murphy sets a moderate, sustainable pace on the flat Polytrack circuit, corners efficiently and kicks clear before hold-up horses can organise a challenge; the Standard to Slow surface blunts late acceleration and makes it very hard to reel in a well-rated front-runner conserving energy.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Chase Cloud Forest Down
scenarios.trigger: If Cuff It or Church Wedding track Cloud Forest tightly and use their proximity to collar the leader inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: One of the close-tracking prominent types benefits from sitting second or third throughout, exerting sustained pressure without launching a wide sweeping move; the flat finish rewards those who have saved ground on the bend rather than those storming home from off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closer Steals Modest Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Cloud Forest sets a genuinely slow early gallop that compresses the field and invites midfield horses to quicken on the turn.
scenarios.body: A horse racing in the first half of the field capitalises on the bunched order and quickens to the front before the straight; Kudos Too or Shadow Road, able to switch off and produce a turn of foot, are best placed if the pace is truly dawdling.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is genuinely fast enough to cause front-runners to tie up in the straight, gifting deep closers a clear run.
scenarios.body: No Ordinary Joe or Dove Tale would need a much stronger-than-expected pace to burn off the leaders plus a clean passage — both are tagged as faders and a flat circuit with a slow surface makes this scenario the least likely; the redistribution of Angel Breeze away from its natural hold-up role further reduces the probability of this shape delivering.

watchPoints.text: Cloud Forest's ability to slide through the race completely unmolested is the single biggest factor — if Murphy is allowed to bowl along at a leisurely pace and coast into the straight, hold-up horses such as No Ordinary Joe and Dove Tale have no conceivable path to victory on this flat track.

Church Wedding and Cuff It will contest the prominent positions directly behind Cloud Forest; whichever of the two settles closer and corners more efficiently on the final bend is likely to emerge as the main danger, making their early positioning in the first two furlongs crucial to watch.

Angel Breeze returns after 252 days off the track and has two AW runs of 9th and 14th to her name — monitor her in the parade ring and early exchanges; if she bounces outward at the start or gets detached early she becomes irrelevant to the finish.

The Standard to Slow going condition has been consistent across all eight races on the card, confirming a genuine surface drag — this systematically disadvantages all hold-up horses requiring a sharp late burst and should be factored into any assessment of No Ordinary Joe, Dove Tale and Kudos Too.

Wreck It Ronnie carries no form data and an unknown running style — watch for any market move in the final minutes as the only clue to how connections rate the debutant's readiness; an unexpected gamble would merit attention given the trainer's otherwise cold 14-day record.

races.name: Unibet Supporting Safer Gambling Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Jumeirah Sands
runners_data.note: Five wins and places from five runs on Standard Kempton-equivalent surfaces is the standout course-going angle here; Kyle McHugh claims 7lb, offsetting the OR-81 weight, and a prominent, forward-pressing style suits the likely race shape perfectly.
runners_data.comment: Jumeirah Sands shaped with plenty of promise when second two starts back and has prior experience of today's trip and going to call on; she was also a winner three starts back, and at 22 days since her last outing she arrives fresh enough to go well from stall six off 136 lb.

runners_data.name: Angel Gabriel
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's 3yo is the lone front-runner, and Rossa Ryan's booking is a clear upgrade; only 2/5 runners on comparable going is a mild concern, but uncontested lead-setting on a flat track is a powerful tactical advantage.
runners_data.comment: Angel Gabriel lands a career-best effort two starts back and returns here in decent order off a 26-day break, carrying 135 lb from stall 3 with distance experience to call on — the main concern is that eighth last time out leaves form to recapture.

runners_data.name: Captain Fox
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes' colt ran creditably in better company and his 7f Kempton form (2nd last time at this course/distance on Standard) is directly relevant; races prominently and will be travelling just off the pace, making him a logical threat to the leader in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Captain Fox won three starts back and has experience of today's distance and going, giving him a solid platform to threaten from stall 8 off 134 lb; the worry is that back-to-back fifth and sixth placed finishes since suggest he's having to find his very best form.

runners_data.name: Piscean Star
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride which is an obvious talent injection, and the horse has a win and second from three starts on Standard Kempton-style surfaces; the 321-day absence after just three career starts is the only meaningful flag — fitness on reappearance must be assumed rather than proven.
runners_data.comment: A 321-day absence makes Piscean Star extremely hard to fancy on return, and he ranks seventh of eight on our figures. He does hold distance and going experience, and a win three starts back offers a glimmer, but the lengthy layoff is the dominant concern.

runners_data.name: Quadrillion
runners_data.note: Colin Keane partnership is attractive and the horse has placed twice from three starts on Good ground, but its natural prominent racing style means it is squeezed out of that position in this field; racing in a less comfortable midfield role tempers its prospects, regardless of ability.
runners_data.comment: Placed twice in her last three starts — second two starts back and third three starts back — Quadrillion heads here winless but with experience over today's trip; a 56-day break and a mark of 75 leave questions, though 130 lb from stall 2 adds another consideration.

runners_data.name: Blakefell
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's runner has no wins or places from its sole Standard-going start, which is a genuine concern on tonight's surface; though a naturally prominent sort, it is pushed into midfield by the crowded pace bracket and its recent form string lacks the consistency to inspire confidence here.
runners_data.comment: Blakefell was third last time out and a winner three starts back, and he has run over today's trip and going — our rating has him joint top-rated in this field. The concern is a trainer firing at just 4% over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Victory Ace
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins on artificial surfaces and a very recent run 11 days ago suggests fitness is spot on; the hood (headgear noted) and hold-up style mean it needs the pace to be genuinely strong to close, and a controlled Angel Gabriel-led race may not provide enough of a target.
runners_data.comment: Victory Ace won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, but his record in the last five starts also includes a fifth and a sixth, and 130 lb is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Doodling
runners_data.note: Callum Hutchinson takes over for Eve Johnson Houghton, whose yard has placed three from 32 over 14 days — active but not red-hot; 53 days off and a recent form string of disappointing efforts at this trip on Standard suggest the market will price the chance fairly.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Doodling's recent form is patchy — sixth, eighth, and seventh in three of her last four starts — though she did score last time out and has experience of today's distance and going.

races.paceDynamic: Angel Gabriel is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger likely to contest the lead aggressively, Rossa Ryan can dictate a controlled, honest gallop from the front on the all-weather at Kempton over 7f. Jumeirah Sands and Captain Fox will press from prominent positions just behind, ensuring the pace is real but not suicidal — Standard To Slow going will further encourage a measured tempo rather than a sprint. The field holds more prominent-minded types than can all secure their natural position: Quadrillion and Blakefell are genuine press-the-pace horses but are mapped to midfield given the crowded prominent bracket, meaning they must settle for a less natural role. This race shape — a single unhurried leader, modest honest fractions on a stamina-testing surface — strongly favours horses who can travel prominently or in the first half of the field and sustain their effort into the rising finish, rather than those relying on a late burst from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Angel Gabriel Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Angel Gabriel dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the prominent pack fails to quicken past him in the straight.
scenarios.body: Angel Gabriel gets an uncontested lead at his own pace, conserving energy through the bend, and Ralph Beckett's 3yo simply finds more in the final furlong than rivals who have been chasing without ever landing a blow; Rossa Ryan is well placed to judge the fractions on this flat Kempton layout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Surge Late
scenarios.trigger: If a genuinely honest pace is set and Jumeirah Sands or Captain Fox track Angel Gabriel closely before asserting in the final 2f.
scenarios.body: The slightly elevated fractions take enough out of Angel Gabriel that one or both of the tracking prominent horses find a decisive turn of foot inside the final furlong; Jumeirah Sands' excellent record on Standard Kempton turf equivalent going and Captain Fox's course form make them the logical beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Sweeps Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or over-heats sufficiently to leave a gap for Victory Ace or Doodling to pick up late ground.
scenarios.body: Victory Ace has back-to-back wins on artificial surfaces and carries headgear, giving John Butler's runner the tactical speed to pick off tiring leaders; Doodling is most exposed on recent form but returns after 53 days and Eve Johnson Houghton's yard is in form, giving it an each-way profile if the shape opens up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If pace flares early with Quadrillion and Blakefell failing to settle in midfield and forcing an unusually strong gallop that plays havoc with all projections.
scenarios.body: Should either displaced prominent type struggle for cover and push forward into a faster-than-expected pace, the race shape collapses into chaos, compressing the field and making the result hard to read; even so, this fractured shape would most likely hand the race back to a truly prominent horse who avoids the early skirmish rather than rewarding the true hold-up runners.

watchPoints.text: Angel Gabriel's ability to lead unchallenged from the start is the pivotal factor — if anything forces Rossa Ryan to use up early, the entire race shape changes and the probability of Scenario A collapses immediately.

Quadrillion and Blakefell are natural front-runners mapped to midfield — watch the early stages to see if either pushes forward regardless, which could ignite an unexpectedly strong pace and blow up the settled lead scenario.

Piscean Star's 321-day absence means Oisin Murphy will be under instructions to educate rather than win at all costs — if the horse is race-fit it is a serious player, but blind faith in the Murphy booking alone is a risk given the layoff.

Standard To Slow going is slower than the listed Standard surface — any horse with a profile built on fast-ground speed (Angel Gabriel's two wins came on Soft/Standard) should be monitored in the market for late drifts that signal trainer concern.

Victory Ace ran just 11 days ago and returns in headgear — watch whether the market supports a quick turnaround angle, as John Butler's record of 3/19 over 14 days suggests the yard sends horses fit to run rather than to make up the numbers.

races.name: Unibet More Extra Place Races Handicap Stakes (London Stayers' Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Tuba
runners_data.note: Hugely progressive stayer in excellent form (three wins in last six including back-to-back 14f wins on Standard), races prominently and will sit just behind the leaders from the front — the step up to 2m looks a natural fit for a horse with a stout profile and consistent course-going record.|
runners_data.comment: Tuba arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and has run over today's trip, making conditions familiar; the 47-day break is the one query, but his recent form is the standout argument for his claims here off 142 lb.

runners_data.name: Roland Garros
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who will try to lead, but his sim-going record of just 1 comparable run from 15 with zero wins and zeros places on similar surfaces is a significant concern; Alexandra Egan's 7lb claim helps but this is the acid test of his stamina.|
runners_data.comment: Roland Garros won two starts back but has posted a seventh last time out and a fifth three starts back, suggesting inconsistency; he has the fitness of a 35-day break and carries 141 lb, which will test his resolve.

runners_data.name: Easter Icon
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a course win at 19f on Good and proven at 22f, 56 days off for trainer Gary Brown who has minimal runners — the layoff and the sharp end of a stayers' handicap will need careful watching but the trip suits his profile.|
runners_data.comment: Easter Icon won two of his last four starts, with back-to-back victories two and three starts back, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions — the main concern is whether 56 days off the track has left him short of peak sharpness.

runners_data.name: Captain Robert
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse fitted with a hood, stepping up significantly in trip to 2m having been placed six times from 10 runs including a win on Soft — Fanshawe's 2/18 recent strike rate is modest but this horse runs well fresh (56 days off) and the longer trip may finally unlock his best.|
runners_data.comment: Captain Robert won last time out but has been beaten in four of his last five starts in recent form, and our rating ranks him seventh of eight in this field — hard to make a case for him despite the distance experience and a return to form last time.

runners_data.name: Golden Garden
runners_data.note: True hold-up type fitted with a tongue-strap, stepping up to 2m having never raced beyond 16f and with all recent outings on Good ground — the combination of an unproven stamina ceiling and no confirmed form on Standard to Slow is the primary concern for De Sousa to manage.|
runners_data.comment: Golden Garden showed what he's capable of with a win in his recent starts, and he has going experience to call on; the main concern is that he hasn't run in 61 days and his last three outings have all been disappointments.

runners_data.name: V Power
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in good recent form with a win 29 days ago at 14f on Standard and three wins from 15 in similar going — the 2m trip is a new test and the tongue-tie suggests a horse that needs to be kept up to its work, but the live recent form counts.|
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and has run over today's going, but V Power has been inconsistent in recent starts — a third three starts back sandwiched between a fifth and a win — and carrying 136 lb won't help his chance of following up.

runners_data.name: Desert Belle
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced 3-year-old trained by Sir Mark Prescott with an unbeaten record of 6/6 in comparable going conditions and consistent frame-finishes at 12-14f — stepping up to 2m from 14f is the key question mark, but Prescott's preparation record at this level is formidable and the p-headgear suggests she's managed with care.|
runners_data.comment: Desert Belle has been placed in five of her last six starts, with a win five starts back, and has experience of today's going — a strong profile backed by a trainer firing at 32% recently. The worry is she carries 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Individualiste
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by profile whose true racing position is at the rear of the field — placed into the midfield mapping because the field is already stacked with hold-up types, but a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.91 tempers confidence; the horse's sim-going record of 0 wins from 15 comparable runs is telling.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a fourth last time out followed by an eighth and ninth in the three starts before that, Individualiste ranks last on our figures here and looks hard to fancy, though he has run over today's distance and going and returns after a 38-day break.

races.paceDynamic: Roland Garros and Desert Belle are the two confirmed front-runners in this eight-runner 2m contest over Kempton's flat Polytrack, and with both likely to want to control proceedings, there will be a genuine battle for the lead from the outset rather than a procession. The Standard to Slow surface will keep the tempo honest rather than electric, meaning the fractions are unlikely to be truly punishing, but the sustained nature of two miles on this track will still test stamina as the field rounds into the home straight. Tuba and Easter Icon will press from prominent positions just off the duelling leaders, creating a multi-layered front end that squeezes the oxygen out of any lone front-runner's advantage and prevents either Roland Garros or Desert Belle from stealing a breather. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all comfortably secure their natural positions — Desert Belle, with Sir Mark Prescott's well-executed campaign behind her and six from six in similar going, is best placed to control the lead, while Roland Garros is most likely to press and force the pace. This contested, honest gallop on a surface that rewards those who travel well through the race favours the hold-up and late-sweeping profiles, with Captain Robert and Golden Garden the styles most likely to benefit if the front end burns itself out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead Burns Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Roland Garros and Desert Belle push each other through genuinely honest fractions over the first mile, creating a race that stretches the field and rewards those who conserve energy.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners trade blows through the middle portion of the race, gradually sapping the stamina of the prominent horses pressing close behind, and the race opens up in the straight for those who have been travelling within themselves.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Desert Belle Controls Solo
scenarios.trigger: If Desert Belle's superior course form and Prescott placement allows her to slip the field from the front without Roland Garros matching her stride for stride.
scenarios.body: Desert Belle dictates a controlled, measured pace that suits her stamina profile perfectly, and none of the hold-up horses find sufficient ground to close in the straight on a horse that has finished in the frame in all six starts on similar going.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is compressed and the front end slows enough that Tuba and Easter Icon, tracking close, gain first run turning for home without the leaders burning themselves out.
scenarios.body: Tuba, in excellent recent form with three wins from recent starts including back-to-back wins at 14f on Standard going, and Easter Icon press past the tiring front-runners before the hold-up horses can get organised, rewarding those who raced handy throughout.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Best
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is unexpectedly fast early and the entire front group ties up in the final quarter-mile, leaving late ground for genuine hold-up types.
scenarios.body: V Power and Captain Robert, both with recent wins at shorter trips on Standard going, find room to finish strongly but the redistribution of Individualiste — a true hold-up horse mapped to midfield — means the genuine staying closers are fewer in number than they appear and the scenario is harder to execute than it looks.

watchPoints.text: Desert Belle and Roland Garros — watch the opening furlong closely to see which establishes the lead; if Desert Belle goes unchallenged to the front, the dynamic shifts sharply toward Scenario B and away from a contested burn.
Tuba's weight of 142lbs is the highest in the field — if the Standard to Slow surface adds additional energy cost through 2m, the top weight could be vulnerable late despite excellent recent form.

Golden Garden has not raced beyond 16f and all five recent runs have been on Good ground — watch for any signs of the horse failing to relax or getting outpaced if the hold-up plan requires more stamina than he has demonstrated.

Captain Robert's hood (b) is fitted for the first time or returned to — monitor his behaviour in the early stages; if he settles well behind the contested leaders, his proven ability at 16f on Standard gives him a legitimate staying platform to close from.

The Standard to Slow going at 2m is the slowest surface of the evening card — pace projections for the final quarter-mile should account for meaningful deceleration, which may compress finishing margins and reward those who take a closer position than their natural style suggests.
